newsitem.title: JAPAN: BOJ money policy aiming to help recovery--governor.
newsitem.headline: BOJ money policy aiming to help recovery--governor.

text.p: Bank of Japan Governor Yasuo Matsushita said on Friday that the central bank's monetary policy would continue to be aimed at ensuring a firm basis for economic recovery.
Japan's economy is recovering gradually, Matsushita said at a meeting of business executives.
However, capital spending and private consumption must strengthen further for Japan's economy to achieve an autonomous recovery.
"The BOJ's monetary policy will continue to be geared to making a firmer basis for economic recovery," he said.
The BOJ cut its official discount rate to a historic low of 0.5 percent in September last year, and low interest rates have helped the economy recover, he said.
Matsushita also said that the pace of decrease in net exports is losing momentum due to the correction of the yen's rise.
"The correction of the yen's strength from last year is showing an impact on both exports and imports, and the tempo of (net export) decrease is showing signs of slowing down," Matsushita said.
